item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Our glorious, magnanimous lord Dmatix decides he wants to share his opinions regarding Resurrection and other stuff on the wiki with us. To do this, he creates a character called Observer who he can write about, and through that writing, convey his own beliefs, essentially puppeteering Observer into saying what he wants to say about stuff on the site- like most writers do when using a character to express themselves. Implied is the fact that Observer has some degree of sapience and capability of free thought, but is still controlled by Dmatix's stories. Observer, bound to the will of Dmatix's typing fingers, cynically watches the Foundation, commenting on characters such as Clef and Iris/Able, making judgments on them while believing those judgments to be his own opinions, not Dmatix's. At the end, Observer realizes that he really is nothing more than a mouthpiece for Dmatix, and that nothing he has done or will do or thinks or will think is of his own creation, it's all controlled by the author, Dmatix, and he is as helpless as all the other characters in the Foundationverse.
Ayup.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Fantastic piece of writing. It's so very hard to do meta in a way that isn't obnoxiously in your face to some extent, and we have some meta that is so in your face that the author just jumped clear down the reader's throat in hopes of getting to the other side and finding upvotes there. But this is metafiction done with a certain elegance to it, a certain grace. Enthusiastic upvote.
